easy.def: A word for you and other people together.
examples: We are friends.
We play ball after school.
Today we sing a song.

more.def: A word a speaker or writer uses for themselves and one or more other people.
examples: We planted tomatoes in the garden last spring.
In our town, we celebrate with a parade every summer.
If we work together, we can finish this faster.

easy.def: Not strong.
examples: The baby is weak.
The rope was weak.
A weak branch.

more.def: Not having much strength.
examples: The weak branch snapped in the wind.
He felt weak after being sick.
The tea was weak and watery.

easy.def: To become less strong or to make something less strong.
examples: The storm weakened the tree.
Illness can weaken you.
The sun weakens the color.

more.def: To make something less strong, or to become less strong.
examples: The storm weakened the old tree.
Being sick can weaken you for a few days.
The sun weakened the color of the paint over time.

easy.def: In a way that is not strong.
examples: He smiled weakly.
She waved weakly.
The bird chirped weakly.

more.def: In a way that has little strength or force.
examples: He smiled weakly after being sick all week.
The kitten meowed weakly from the box.
"I'm fine," she said weakly.

easy.def: Not being strong.
examples: The illness left her with weakness.
His weakness was in his arm.
Weakness made it hard to lift.

more.def: A lack of strength, or something you are not good at.
examples: The illness left her with weakness in her legs.
Spelling is my weakness.
Cookies are his weakness, and he cannot say no.

easy.def: Having lots of money and things.
examples: The king had great wealth.
She had wealth.
Wealth is not everything.

more.def: A large amount of money or valuable things.
examples: The king had great wealth and many castles.
The pirates counted their wealth.
Friends are worth more than wealth.

easy.def: Having a lot of money.
examples: The wealthy queen had lots of gold.
The wealthy man had a big house.
She is wealthy but lives simply.

more.def: Having a lot of money or valuable things; rich.
examples: A wealthy family gave money to build the new library.
The wealthy merchant owned ten ships.
It is one of the wealthiest cities in the world.

easy.def: Something used to fight or hurt.
examples: A sword is a weapon.
Knights carried weapons.
Soldiers have weapons.

more.def: An object used to fight or to hurt someone.
examples: A sword is a weapon from long ago.
The knights carried weapons into battle.
Some animals use horns as weapons.

easy.def: To have clothes on your body.
examples: I wear a hat.
She wore a red dress.
He wears glasses.

more.def: To have clothes, shoes, or jewelry on your body.
examples: I wear boots when it snows.
She wore a silver necklace to the party.
Everyone must wear a helmet when riding a bike.

easy.def: A person who wears something.
examples: The wearer of the hat.
Each wearer gets a tag.
The wearer smiled.

more.def: A person who wears a certain thing.
examples: The wearer of the hat smiled at us.
Each wearer of glasses got a case.
The wearer of the costume won a prize.

easy.def: In a very tired way.
examples: He sat down wearily.
She wearily walked home.
The dog wearily lay down.

more.def: In a tired way, often after working hard or a long time.
examples: The hikers walked wearily up the last hill.
She wearily rubbed her eyes after the long trip.
The farmer wearily climbed down from the tractor.

easy.def: Very tired.
examples: The weary boy fell asleep.
The weary dog lay down.
I am weary after the long day.

more.def: Very tired, especially after working hard or for a long time.
examples: The weary travelers were glad to finally reach the inn.
The weary nurse had worked all night.
She gave a weary sigh and sat down.

easy.def: A small, thin animal with a long body.
examples: The weasel is quick.
A weasel hid in the hole.
The weasel has short legs.

more.def: A small animal with a long, thin body and short legs that hunts mice and birds.
examples: The weasel slipped through the hole.
A weasel is quick and thin.
The weasel hunted mice in the field.

easy.def: What it is like outside, like sunny or rainy.
examples: The weather is sunny today.
We play inside in bad weather.
I like snowy weather.

more.def: What the air outside is like at a certain time, such as hot, cold, rainy, or windy.
examples: We checked the weather before planning our picnic.
The game was called off because of bad weather.
The weather in the mountains can change quickly.

easy.def: A person on TV who tells about the weather.
examples: The weatherman said it will rain.
I watched the weatherman.
The weatherman was right.

more.def: A person whose job is to report and explain the weather, usually on television or radio.
examples: The weatherman said it would snow by morning.
The weatherman showed a map with clouds and rain.
We listened to the weatherman before we planned the picnic.

easy.def: To make cloth by crossing threads over and under.
examples: She weaves a basket.
Grandma weaves cloth.
They wove a rug.

more.def: To make cloth or baskets by passing strips or threads over and under one another.
examples: She wove a basket from long grasses.
Grandma weaves wool into cloth on her loom.
The spider weaves a web between the branches.

easy.def: To move around things, going in and out.
examples: The bike weaves between cones.
He wove through the crowd.
The runner weaves.

more.def: To move along a path by turning and going around things.
examples: The bike weaved between the cones.
He wove through the crowd to find his mom.
The road weaves through the hills.

easy.def: A person who makes cloth from thread.
examples: The weaver made a rug.
A weaver uses thread.
The weaver sat at the loom.

more.def: A person whose work is making cloth by crossing threads over and under each other.
examples: The weaver made a colorful rug on her loom.
A weaver can make cloth from wool or cotton.
The village weaver sold blankets at the market.

easy.def: A net that a spider spins.
examples: The spider made a web.
The web is sticky.
A fly is caught in the web.

more.def: A net of thin, sticky threads that a spider spins to catch insects.
examples: The spider spun a web between the branches.
Dew sparkled on the web.
A fly got stuck in the web.

easy.def: The internet.
examples: I looked it up on the web.
The web has many sites.
She searches the web.

more.def: The internet, where people look at pages of information.
examples: I looked up the answer on the web.
The web has pages about every subject.
We used the web for our project.

easy.def: A group of pages on the internet that belong together.
examples: I visited the website.
The website has pictures.
Our school has a website.

more.def: A place on the internet with pages of information about a person, group or topic.
examples: I visited the zoo's website to see the animals.
Our school has a website with the lunch menu.
The website shows pictures of baby penguins.

easy.def: To marry.
examples: They will wed in June.
The two wed in the park.
She wed her best friend.

more.def: To marry someone, or to join together in marriage.
examples: The couple will wed in the garden next spring.
In the fairy tale, the prince wed the girl in the glass shoes.
They wed in a small ceremony in a church.

easy.def: A party when two people get married.
examples: We went to a wedding.
The wedding was in the park.
She wore a long dress at the wedding.

more.def: A ceremony in which two people get married, usually followed by a celebration.
examples: My cousin's wedding was in a garden.
Everyone danced at the wedding.
The wedding cake had three layers.

easy.def: A piece that is thick at one end and thin at the other.
examples: I ate a wedge of pie.
She put a wedge under the door.
Dad cut a wedge of melon.

more.def: A piece of something shaped like a triangle, thick at one end and thin at the other.
examples: I cut a wedge of cheese.
She put a wooden wedge under the door to hold it open.
A wedge of lemon sat on the side of the glass.

easy.def: To push something into a tight space.
examples: I wedge the book in.
He wedged the door open.
She wedged the box in the car.

more.def: To fit something into a narrow space so that it cannot move.
examples: I wedged the book onto the full shelf.
He wedged a stone under the door to hold it open.
She wedged the box between two seats.

easy.def: The day after Tuesday.
examples: We have music on Wednesday.
My cousin visits on Wednesday.
Wednesday is the middle of the school week.

more.def: The day of the week that comes after Tuesday and before Thursday.
examples: Wednesday is halfway through the school week.
The farmers' market is open every Wednesday.
Our team has soccer practice on Wednesday afternoon.

easy.def: A wild plant that grows where you do not want it.
examples: Weeds grow in the garden.
I pulled a weed.
A weed grew through the crack.

more.def: A wild plant that grows where people do not want it to grow.
examples: Weeds grew in the garden between the flowers.
I pulled a weed out of the sidewalk crack.
The farmer pulled the weeds from the corn.

easy.def: Seven days in a row.
examples: A week has seven days.
I see Grandma next week.
We were gone for a week.

more.def: A period of seven days, often from Sunday or Monday to the end of the weekend.
examples: We have art class twice a week.
My cousins will stay with us for a week.
The school fair is held in the last week of May.

easy.def: Any day from Monday to Friday.
examples: Monday is a weekday.
We go to school on weekdays.
Weekdays are busy.

more.def: A day of the week that is not Saturday or Sunday.
examples: Most stores are open on weekdays, but some close on Sunday.
The library is open every weekday.
Weekdays start with Monday.

easy.def: Saturday and Sunday.
examples: We play on the weekend.
The weekend is fun.
See you this weekend.

more.def: Saturday and Sunday, the days when many people do not work or go to school.
examples: We go hiking on the weekend.
She visits her grandma every weekend.
The weekend was rainy.

easy.def: Happening once each week.
examples: We have a weekly spelling test.
I get a weekly allowance.
The weekly meeting is on Monday.

more.def: Done or happening once every week.
examples: Our class has a weekly trip to the library on Fridays.
The town sends out a weekly newspaper about local news.
She goes to her weekly piano lesson on Tuesday afternoon.

easy.def: One time each week.
examples: We have art weekly.
The mail comes weekly.
She calls Grandma weekly.

more.def: Once every week; each week.
examples: The club meets weekly in the school gym.
The paper is printed weekly and delivered on Sundays.
He waters the plants weekly during the summer.

easy.def: Very, very small.
examples: A weeny ant.
The weeny bug.
I have a weeny bit.

more.def: Very small; tiny.
examples: A weeny ant crawled across the page.
She ate a weeny piece of cake.
He held a weeny shell in his palm.

easy.def: To cry.
examples: She wept.
I weep at sad movies.
The child wept.

more.def: To cry, shedding tears.
examples: She wept when she heard the sad news.
The little boy wept when his kite broke.
We wept at the end of the sad movie.

easy.def: Ready to cry.
examples: The baby is weepy.
I feel weepy.
A weepy movie.

more.def: Ready to cry, or making you cry.
examples: The baby felt weepy and tired.
I felt weepy at the sad part of the movie.
The weepy child needed a hug.

easy.def: A small bug that eats plants.
examples: A weevil ate the grain.
The weevil is small.
Weevils are bugs.

more.def: A small beetle with a long snout that eats plants and stored food.
examples: A weevil bored into the seed.
Weevils can ruin a crop of cotton.
The weevil has a long, curved snout.

easy.def: To find how heavy something is.
examples: I weigh the apples.
She weighed the box.
The scale weighs me.

more.def: To measure how heavy something is, or to be a certain heaviness.
examples: The cashier weighed the apples.
I weigh about sixty pounds.
The baby weighs eight pounds.

easy.def: How heavy something is.
examples: The weight of the box is ten pounds.
The baby's weight is up.
Check your weight.

more.def: A measure of how heavy something is.
examples: The weight of the suitcase was twenty pounds.
The bridge can hold a lot of weight.
The baby's weight went up.

easy.def: A heavy object.
examples: He lifts weights.
The weight dropped.
A weight on the scale.

more.def: A heavy object used for exercise or to hold things down.
examples: He lifts weights at the gym.
A weight held the paper down.
The scale uses a small weight.

easy.def: Very strange.
examples: What a weird noise!
It is weird that it snowed in May.
The dream was weird.

more.def: Very strange or unusual, and hard to explain.
examples: I heard a weird noise outside my window.
It felt weird to be at school with no one else there.
The weather was weird, with snow in May.

easy.def: In a strange way.
examples: The cat acted weirdly.
It was weirdly quiet.
He walked weirdly.

more.def: In a strange and unusual way.
examples: The cat was acting weirdly all morning.
It was weirdly quiet in the park.
The sky glowed weirdly before the storm.

easy.def: Being strange.
examples: The weirdness of the dream.
I felt the weirdness.
The weirdness was funny.

more.def: The quality of being strange or unusual.
examples: The weirdness of the dream made me laugh.
I loved the weirdness of the old house.
The weirdness of the story kept us guessing.

easy.def: A friendly word you say when someone arrives.
examples: Welcome to our home!
Welcome! Come in.
Welcome to school, class!

more.def: Used to greet someone in a friendly way when they arrive.
examples: Welcome to the library! Let me show you around.
Welcome back, everyone! I hope you had a good summer.
Welcome aboard! Please find your seat.

easy.def: To say hello in a happy way.
examples: We welcome our guests.
Dad welcomed Grandma at the door.
The class welcomed the new girl.

more.def: To greet someone with kindness when they arrive.
examples: The mayor welcomed the visitors to our town.
Our neighbors welcomed us with a basket of muffins.
The puppy welcomed me home by wagging its tail.

easy.def: Wanted and liked.
examples: You are always welcome here.
A cold drink is welcome on a hot day.
Rain is welcome in the dry garden.

more.def: Gladly received or accepted, making people happy.
examples: The cool breeze was a welcome change after the long, hot walk.
Visitors are always welcome at our school.
After the long drive, a snack was welcome.

easy.def: To join pieces of metal by heating them.
examples: He welds the metal.
The worker welded the pipe.
They weld the bars.

more.def: To join pieces of metal together by heating them until they melt and fuse.
examples: The worker welded the two pipes together.
He welded a new bar onto the gate.
They weld metal to build ships.

easy.def: A person who joins metal using heat.
examples: The welder joined the metal.
A welder wears a mask.
The welder made sparks.

more.def: A person whose job is to join pieces of metal together by heating them.
examples: The welder wore a mask to protect his eyes.
A welder joined the steel beams.
The welder fixed the broken gate.

easy.def: Joining metal by melting it with heat.
examples: Welding joins metal.
He does welding.
The welding made sparks.

more.def: The process of joining pieces of metal by heating them until they melt together.
examples: Welding joins two pieces of metal together.
He does welding in a factory.
Sparks flew from the welding.

easy.def: Good health and happiness.
examples: We care about the welfare of animals.
Her welfare is important.
He checks on the welfare of the dog.

more.def: The good health, safety and happiness of a person or animal.
examples: The vet takes care of the welfare of the animals.
Parents worry about the welfare of their children.
The class made a plan to protect the welfare of the pond animals.

easy.def: In a good way.
examples: She sings well.
He did well on the test.
I slept well.

more.def: In a good or successful way, or in a thorough way.
examples: The team played well and won the game.
Mix the paint well before you use it.
Our dog listens well when we call her.

easy.def: Not sick.
examples: I feel well today.
Are you well now?
Grandma is well again.

more.def: In good health.
examples: I stayed home from school until I was well again.
The doctor said the baby is well and growing fast.
You do not look well, so you should rest.

easy.def: A deep hole in the ground with water in it.
examples: We got water from the well.
A bucket hangs in the well.
The well is very deep.

more.def: A deep hole dug into the ground to reach water, oil, or gas.
examples: Long ago, villagers carried buckets of water from the well.
The farmer dug a new well near the barn.
Oil comes from a deep well that goes far under the ground.

easy.def: A person in scary stories who turns into a wolf.
examples: The werewolf howled.
The movie had a werewolf.
I dressed as a werewolf.

more.def: A creature in scary stories who is a person by day and turns into a wolf at night.
examples: The werewolf howled at the full moon.
The movie had a scary werewolf.
He wore a werewolf mask for Halloween.

easy.def: The direction where the sun goes down.
examples: The sun sets in the west.
We drove west.
Birds flew west.

more.def: The direction opposite to east, where the sun sets.
examples: Storms often roll in from the west.
We drove west toward the mountains.
Pioneers traveled west in wagons.

easy.def: Going toward the west.
examples: The westbound train left.
I saw a westbound road.
The westbound bus is late.

more.def: Traveling or leading toward the west.
examples: The westbound train left the station.
We took the westbound road.
The westbound lanes were busy.

easy.def: Having to do with the west.
examples: The western sky was red.
The western side of the town is quiet.
She lives in the western part of the state.

more.def: Facing or coming from the west, the direction where the sun sets.
examples: The sky in the western part of the country was clear.
The western side of the house gets the evening sun.
A western wind blew in from the sea.

easy.def: A person from the west.
examples: A westerner lived there.
The westerner rode a horse.
He is a westerner.

more.def: A person who comes from the west of a country or the world.
examples: The westerner wore a cowboy hat.
A westerner visited the city.
The westerners traveled across the plains.

easy.def: Toward the west.
examples: The wagons rolled westward.
The sun sets westward.
We drove westward.

more.def: In the direction of the west.
examples: The settlers traveled westward in covered wagons.
The sun slipped westward behind the hills.
We sailed westward across the bay.

easy.def: Covered with water.
examples: The towel is wet.
My hair is wet.
The grass is wet.

more.def: Covered with or soaked in water or another liquid.
examples: Her wet hair dripped on the towel.
The grass was wet with dew.
The wet dog shook itself dry.

easy.def: Land that is covered with water, like a swamp.
examples: Frogs live in the wetland.
The wetland is wet.
We walked by the wetland.

more.def: Low land that is covered with shallow water for part or all of the year.
examples: Frogs and herons live in the wetland.
The wetland soaks up water during floods.
We walked on a boardwalk through the wetland.

easy.def: A tight suit for swimming in cold water.
examples: The diver wore a wetsuit.
My wetsuit is black.
The wetsuit keeps me warm.

more.def: A close-fitting rubber suit that keeps swimmers and divers warm in cold water.
examples: The surfer wore a wetsuit in the chilly water.
A wetsuit traps a thin layer of warm water against the skin.
The diver pulled on a thick wetsuit.
